question:
A 30-year-old nulliparous woman seeks consultation regarding contraception options, specifically
interested in sterilization. Her medical history includes severe endometriosis and chronic pelvic pain,
managed with oral contraceptive pills, and a previous appendectomy for a ruptured appendix. She has
exclusively had female sexual partners and is currently in a monogamous relationship for the past year.
Physical examination reveals a healed 4 cm right lower quadrant incision, and bimanual pelvic
examination demonstrates generalized pelvic tenderness with limited uterine mobility. After receiving
comprehensive contraceptive counseling, the patient expresses interest in exploring long-acting
reversible contraceptive methods. What is the primary contraindication for permanent sterilization in
this case? Answer Choices: (A) Inadequate counseling on alternative methods (B) Sterilization is not

contraindicated in this patient (C) Uncertainty about permanent contraception (D) Severe pelvic
adhesive disease (E) Need for continued endometriosis treatment (F) Age < 25 and lack of living
children (G) Lack of partner consent for sterilization (H) Having exclusively female sexual partners (I)
Current use of hormonal contraception (J) High risk of surgical complications
 A. Sterilization is not contraindicated in this patient
B. Current use of hormonal contraception
C. Severe pelvic adhesive disease
D. Lack of partner consent for sterilization
E. Inadequate counseling on alternative methods
F. Age < 25 and lack of living children
G. Need for continued endometriosis treatment
H. High risk of surgical complications
I. Having exclusively female sexual partners
J. Uncertainty about permanent contraception
